Why do I feel really well rested after less than 5 hours of sleep, but feel groggy and tired when I sleep longer than that?

This is what I remember from my Psychology courses a while back, may have misremembered:

Your sleep cycle alternates between REM (rapid eye movement) sleep, which is when you dream, process new information & are only lightly asleep, and NREM (non-REM) sleep, which is when you "hibernate" and your body rests.

A healthy sleep pattern consists of about four REM and three NREM cycles. The periods of REM gradually decrease in length with each cycle while the periods of NREM get longer. After a fourth NREM cycle, you experience REM for only a very short time.

If you're very groggy when you wake up, you've most likely woken up during a period of NREM sleep. This is known as "deep sleep" because your body typically shuts out any non-intensive stimulus; your body isn't fully 'aware' that you're awake due to the deviation from its natural sleep cycle pattern.

If you have a smartphone, I recommend checking out the 'Sleep Cycle' (and companion 'Power Nap') app. It does its best to wake you up during REM, provided you set a large enough window of time. I've been using it for about a year and it improved my sleep quality quite a bit.
I have had great success with SleepBot. Got me on a good schedule for the past 8 months.

I tried finding out about an article that I read in a newsletter I subscribed to about a similar subject, but I could not find it so take this with a grain of salt, so to speak.

 

Normally your body is in a 90 minute sleep cycle from pre-REM sleep, to REM, and then post-REM sleep where getting less than 5 hours of sleep interrupts the most recent cycle of this sleep (think of as an inverted bell curve,) and thus if one sleep for 4.5 hours, you might well rested at that point in time but your body needs more than that so after awhile, you will begin to feel sleepy, quicker and faster.

 

If one gets more than 5 hours of rest, then you are still interrupting the sleep cycle until you get to 7.5 hours of rest. Anything longer than that, you are forcing your body to go into REM sleep, which it won't able to do naturally. I hope the brief, off-the-cuff, description helps, if at all.
